facts.fact: 作者给笑话下的定义：一条笑话里同时有两个故事，你以为在听的和实际在听的
facts.anchor: One way of thinking about a joke is as two stories: the one you think you’re being told, and the one you’re actually being told.

facts.fact: 「走进酒吧」那类笑话的转折：bar 不是酒吧，而是一根长金属条
facts.anchor: it wasn’t the kind of bar you drink at, it was a long metal thing

facts.fact: knock-knock 笑话同样靠「Who’s there」后的词在结尾被换成另一件事
facts.anchor: It wasn’t ‘Police’, the crime-fighters, it was ‘Police let me in, I need a poo’: an entirely different tale.

facts.fact: Groucho Marx 的名句被当作两句式笑话的范例：先让你以为在讲打猎，第二句才揭示荒诞的真相
facts.anchor: One morning I shot an elephant in my pyjamas. How he got into my pyjamas, I’ll never know

facts.fact: 作者归纳：多数笑话靠意外的转折或揭示成立
facts.anchor: most jokes hinge on an unexpected turn or revelation

facts.fact: 连冒犯性笑话也靠惊喜：你没想到会糟到这个地步
facts.anchor: you weren’t expecting it to be this messed up!

facts.fact: 笑话也能被恶意使用：作为权力的展示、划清群内群外的界线、以及仇恨的潜台词
facts.anchor: Jokes can be used as a display of power

facts.fact: 全章以一条谐音双关（weigh / way）收尾
facts.anchor: where do you weigh a whale? At a whale weigh station.
